   521→// ShadowBranchExists checks if a shadow branch exists for the given base commit.
   522→func (s *GitStore) ShadowBranchExists(baseCommit string) bool {
   523→	shadowBranchName := ShadowBranchNameForCommit(baseCommit)
   524→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   525→	_, err := s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   526→	return err == nil
   527→}
   528→
   529→// DeleteShadowBranch deletes the shadow branch for the given base commit.
   530→func (s *GitStore) DeleteShadowBranch(baseCommit string) error {
   531→	shadowBranchName := ShadowBranchNameForCommit(baseCommit)
   532→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   533→	if err := s.repo.Storer.RemoveReference(refName); err != nil {
   534→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to delete shadow branch %s: %w", shadowBranchName, err)
   535→	}
   536→	return nil
   537→}
   538→
   539→// ShadowBranchNameForCommit returns the shadow branch name for a base commit hash.
   540→// Uses the first ShadowBranchHashLength characters of the commit hash.
   541→func ShadowBranchNameForCommit(baseCommit string) string {
   542→	if len(baseCommit) >= ShadowBranchHashLength {
   543→		return ShadowBranchPrefix + baseCommit[:ShadowBranchHashLength]
   544→	}
   545→	return ShadowBranchPrefix + baseCommit
   546→}
   547→
   548→// getOrCreateShadowBranch gets or creates the shadow branch for checkpoints.
   549→// Returns (parentHash, baseTreeHash, error).
   550→func (s *GitStore) getOrCreateShadowBranch(branchName string) (plumbing.Hash, plumbing.Hash, error) {
   551→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(branchName)
   552→	ref, err := s.repo.Reference(refName, true)
   553→
   554→	if err == nil {
   555→		// Branch exists
   556→		commit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   557→		if err != nil {
   558→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get commit object: %w", err)
   559→		}
   560→		return ref.Hash(), commit.TreeHash, nil
   561→	}
   562→
   563→	// Branch doesn't exist, use current HEAD's tree as base
   564→	head, err := s.repo.Head()
   565→	if err != nil {
   566→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD: %w", err)
   567→	}
   568→
   569→	headCommit, err := s.repo.CommitObject(head.Hash())
   570→	if err != nil {
   571→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD commit: %w", err)
   572→	}
   573→
   574→	return plumbing.ZeroHash, headCommit.TreeHash, nil
   575→}
   576→
   577→// buildTreeWithChanges builds a git tree with the given changes.
   578→// metadataDir is the relative path for git tree entries, metadataDirAbs is the absolute path
   579→// for filesystem operations (needed when CLI is run from a subdirectory).
   580→func (s *GitStore) buildTreeWithChanges(
   581→	baseTreeHash plumbing.Hash,
   582→	modifiedFiles, deletedFiles []string,
   583→	metadataDir, metadataDirAbs string,
   584→) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   585→	// Get repo root for resolving file paths
   586→	// This is critical because fileExists() and createBlobFromFile() use os.Stat()
   587→	// which resolves relative to CWD. The modifiedFiles are repo-relative paths,
   588→	// so we must resolve them against repo root, not CWD.
   589→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   590→	if err != nil {
   591→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get repo root: %w", err)
   592→	}
   593→
   594→	// Get the base tree
   595→	baseTree, err := s.repo.TreeObject(baseTreeHash)
   596→	if err != nil {
   597→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to get base tree: %w", err)
   598→	}
   599→
   600→	// Flatten existing tree
   601→	entries := make(map[string]object.TreeEntry)
   602→	if err := FlattenTree(s.repo, baseTree, "", entries); err != nil {
   603→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to flatten base tree: %w", err)
   604→	}
   605→
   606→	// Remove deleted files
   607→	for _, file := range deletedFiles {
   608→		delete(entries, file)
   609→	}
   610→
   611→	// Add/update modified files
   612→	for _, file := range modifiedFiles {
   613→		// Resolve path relative to repo root for filesystem operations
   614→		absPath := filepath.Join(repoRoot, file)
   615→		if !fileExists(absPath) {
   616→			delete(entries, file)
   617→			continue
   618→		}
   619→
   620→		blobHash, mode, err := createBlobFromFile(s.repo, absPath)
   621→		if err != nil {
   622→			// Skip files that can't be staged (may have been deleted since detection)
   623→			continue
   624→		}
   625→
   626→		entries[file] = object.TreeEntry{
   627→			Name: file,
   628→			Mode: mode,
   629→			Hash: blobHash,
   630→		}
   631→	}
   632→
   633→	// Add metadata directory files
   634→	if metadataDir != "" && metadataDirAbs != "" {
   635→		if err := addDirectoryToEntriesWithAbsPath(s.repo, metadataDirAbs, metadataDir, entries); err != nil {
   636→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to add metadata directory: %w", err)
   637→		}
   638→	}
   639→
   640→	// Build tree
   641→	return BuildTreeFromEntries(s.repo, entries)
   642→}
   643→
   644→// createCommit creates a commit object.
   645→func (s *GitStore) createCommit(treeHash, parentHash plumbing.Hash, message, authorName, authorEmail string) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   646→	now := time.Now()
   647→	sig := object.Signature{
   648→		Name:  authorName,
   649→		Email: authorEmail,
   650→		When:  now,
   651→	}
   652→
   653→	commit := &object.Commit{
   654→		TreeHash:  treeHash,
   655→		Author:    sig,
   656→		Committer: sig,
   657→		Message:   message,
   658→	}
   659→
   660→	// Add parent if not a new branch
   661→	if parentHash != plumbing.ZeroHash {
   662→		commit.ParentHashes = []plumbing.Hash{parentHash}
   663→	}
   664→
   665→	obj := s.repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   666→	if err := commit.Encode(obj); err != nil {
   667→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to encode commit: %w", err)
   668→	}
   669→
   670→	hash, err := s.repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
   671→	if err != nil {
   672→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to store commit: %w", err)
   673→	}
   674→
   675→	return hash, nil
   676→}
   677→
   678→// Helper functions extracted from strategy/common.go
   679→// These are exported for use by strategy package (push_common.go, session_test.go)
   680→
   681→// FlattenTree recursively flattens a tree into a map of full paths to entries.
   682→func FlattenTree(repo *git.Repository, tree *object.Tree, prefix string, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) error {
   683→	for _, entry := range tree.Entries {
   684→		fullPath := entry.Name
   685→		if prefix != "" {
   686→			fullPath = prefix + "/" + entry.Name
   687→		}
   688→
   689→		if entry.Mode == filemode.Dir {
   690→			// Recurse into subtree
   691→			subtree, err := repo.TreeObject(entry.Hash)
   692→			if err != nil {
   693→				return fmt.Errorf("failed to get subtree %s: %w", fullPath, err)
   694→			}
   695→			if err := FlattenTree(repo, subtree, fullPath, entries); err != nil {
   696→				return err
   697→			}
   698→		} else {
   699→			entries[fullPath] = object.TreeEntry{
   700→				Name: fullPath,
   701→				Mode: entry.Mode,
   702→				Hash: entry.Hash,
   703→			}
   704→		}
   705→	}
   706→	return nil
   707→}
   708→
   709→// fileExists checks if a file exists at the given path.
   710→func fileExists(path string) bool {
   711→	_, err := os.Stat(path)
   712→	return err == nil
   713→}
   714→
   715→// createBlobFromFile creates a blob object from a file in the working directory.
   716→func createBlobFromFile(repo *git.Repository, filePath string) (plumbing.Hash, filemode.FileMode, error) {
   717→	info, err := os.Stat(filePath)
   718→	if err != nil {
   719→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to stat file: %w", err)
   720→	}
   721→
   722→	// Determine file mode
   723→	mode := filemode.Regular
   724→	if info.Mode()&0o111 != 0 {
   725→		mode = filemode.Executable
   726→	}
   727→	if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
   728→		mode = filemode.Symlink
   729→	}
   730→
   731→	// Read file contents
   732→	content, err := os.ReadFile(filePath) //nolint:gosec // filePath comes from walking the repository
   733→	if err != nil {
   734→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to read file: %w", err)
   735→	}
   736→
   737→	// Create blob object
   738→	obj := repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   739→	obj.SetType(plumbing.BlobObject)
   740→	obj.SetSize(int64(len(content)))
   741→
   742→	writer, err := obj.Writer()
   743→	if err != nil {
   744→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to get object writer: %w", err)
   745→	}
   746→
   747→	_, err = writer.Write(content)
   748→	if err != nil {
   749→		_ = writer.Close()
   750→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to write blob content: %w", err)
   751→	}
   752→	if err := writer.Close(); err != nil {
   753→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to close blob writer: %w", err)
   754→	}
   755→
   756→	hash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
   757→	if err != nil {
   758→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to store blob object: %w", err)
   759→	}
   760→
   761→	return hash, mode, nil
   762→}
   763→
   764→// addDirectoryToEntriesWithAbsPath recursively adds all files in a directory to the entries map.
   765→func addDirectoryToEntriesWithAbsPath(repo *git.Repository, dirPathAbs, dirPathRel string, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) error {
   766→	err := filepath.Walk(dirPathAbs, func(path string, info os.FileInfo, err error) error {
   767→		if err != nil {
   768→			return err
   769→		}
   770→		if info.IsDir() {
   771→			return nil
   772→		}
   773→
   774→		// Calculate relative path within the directory, then join with dirPathRel for tree entry
   775→		relWithinDir, err := filepath.Rel(dirPathAbs, path)
   776→		if err != nil {
   777→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to get relative path for %s: %w", path, err)
   778→		}
   779→
   780→		blobHash, mode, err := createBlobFromFile(repo, path)
   781→		if err != nil {
   782→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to create blob for %s: %w", path, err)
   783→		}
   784→
   785→		treePath := filepath.Join(dirPathRel, relWithinDir)
   786→		entries[treePath] = object.TreeEntry{
   787→			Name: treePath,
   788→			Mode: mode,
   789→			Hash: blobHash,
   790→		}
   791→		return nil
   792→	})
   793→	if err != nil {
   794→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to walk directory %s: %w", dirPathAbs, err)
   795→	}
   796→	return nil
   797→}
   798→
   799→// treeNode represents a node in our tree structure.
   800→type treeNode struct {
   801→	entries map[string]*treeNode // subdirectories
   802→	files   []object.TreeEntry   // files in this directory
   803→}
   804→
   805→// BuildTreeFromEntries builds a proper git tree structure from flattened file entries.
   806→// Exported for use by strategy package (push_common.go, session_test.go)
   807→func BuildTreeFromEntries(repo *git.Repository, entries map[string]object.TreeEntry) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   808→	// Build a tree structure
   809→	root := &treeNode{
   810→		entries: make(map[string]*treeNode),
   811→		files:   []object.TreeEntry{},
   812→	}
   813→
   814→	// Insert all entries into the tree structure
   815→	for fullPath, entry := range entries {
   816→		parts := strings.Split(fullPath, "/")
   817→		insertIntoTree(root, parts, entry)
   818→	}
   819→
   820→	// Recursively build tree objects from bottom up
   821→	return buildTreeObject(repo, root)
   822→}
   823→
   824→// insertIntoTree inserts a file entry into the tree structure.
   825→func insertIntoTree(node *treeNode, pathParts []string, entry object.TreeEntry) {
   826→	if len(pathParts) == 1 {
   827→		// This is a file in the current directory
   828→		node.files = append(node.files, object.TreeEntry{
   829→			Name: pathParts[0],
   830→			Mode: entry.Mode,
   831→			Hash: entry.Hash,
   832→		})
   833→		return
   834→	}
   835→
   836→	// This is in a subdirectory
   837→	dirName := pathParts[0]
   838→	if node.entries[dirName] == nil {
   839→		node.entries[dirName] = &treeNode{
   840→			entries: make(map[string]*treeNode),
   841→			files:   []object.TreeEntry{},
   842→		}
   843→	}
   844→	insertIntoTree(node.entries[dirName], pathParts[1:], entry)
   845→}
   846→
   847→// buildTreeObject recursively builds tree objects from a treeNode.
   848→func buildTreeObject(repo *git.Repository, node *treeNode) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   849→	var treeEntries []object.TreeEntry
   850→
   851→	// Add files
   852→	treeEntries = append(treeEntries, node.files...)
   853→
   854→	// Recursively build subtrees
   855→	for name, subnode := range node.entries {
   856→		subHash, err := buildTreeObject(repo, subnode)
   857→		if err != nil {
   858→			return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
   859→		}
   860→		treeEntries = append(treeEntries, object.TreeEntry{
   861→			Name: name,
   862→			Mode: filemode.Dir,
   863→			Hash: subHash,
   864→		})
   865→	}
   866→
   867→	// Sort entries (git requires sorted entries)
   868→	sortTreeEntries(treeEntries)
   869→
   870→	// Create tree object
   871→	tree := &object.Tree{Entries: treeEntries}
   872→
   873→	obj := repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
   874→	if err := tree.Encode(obj); err != nil {
   875→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to encode tree: %w", err)
   876→	}
   877→
   878→	hash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
   879→	if err != nil {
   880→		return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("failed to store tree: %w", err)
   881→	}
   882→
   883→	return hash, nil
   884→}
   885→
   886→// sortTreeEntries sorts tree entries in git's required order.
   887→// Git sorts tree entries by name, with directories having a trailing /
   888→func sortTreeEntries(entries []object.TreeEntry) {
   889→	sort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool {
   890→		nameI := entries[i].Name
   891→		nameJ := entries[j].Name
   892→		if entries[i].Mode == filemode.Dir {
   893→			nameI += "/"
   894→		}
   895→		if entries[j].Mode == filemode.Dir {
   896→			nameJ += "/"
   897→		}
   898→		return nameI < nameJ
   899→	})
   900→}
   901→
   902→// collectWorkingDirectoryFiles collects all files in the working directory.
   903→// Excludes .git/ and .entire/ directories.
   904→func collectWorkingDirectoryFiles() ([]string, error) {
   905→	// Get repository root to walk from there
   906→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   907→	if err != nil {
   908→		repoRoot = "." // Fallback to current directory
   909→	}
   910→
   911→	var files []string
   912→	err = filepath.Walk(repoRoot, func(path string, info os.FileInfo, walkErr error) error {
   913→		if walkErr != nil {
   914→			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Skip filesystem errors during walk
   915→		}
   916→
   917→		// Get path relative to repo root
   918→		relPath, err := filepath.Rel(repoRoot, path)
   919→		if err != nil {
   920→			return nil //nolint:nilerr // Skip paths we can't make relative
   921→		}
   922→
   923→		// Skip directories
   924→		if info.IsDir() {
   925→			// Skip .git and .entire directories
   926→			if relPath == gitDir || relPath == entireDir ||
   927→				strings.HasPrefix(relPath, gitDir+"/") || strings.HasPrefix(relPath, entireDir+"/") {
   928→				return filepath.SkipDir
   929→			}
   930→			return nil
   931→		}
   932→
   933→		// Skip files in special directories (shouldn't reach here due to SkipDir, but safety check)
   934→		if strings.HasPrefix(relPath, gitDir+"/") || strings.HasPrefix(relPath, entireDir+"/") {
   935→			return nil
   936→		}
   937→
   938→		files = append(files, relPath)
   939→		return nil
   940→	})
   941→	if err != nil {
   942→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to walk directory: %w", err)
   943→	}
   944→
   945→	return files, nil
   946→}
   947→

> AGENT

That's a cleaner design. The agent knows its transcript format, so it should own the chunking logic. Let me think through the architecture.

Currently there's an import issue:
- `claudecode/transcript.go` imports `checkpoint` for `checkpoint.TokenUsage`
- If checkpoint imports agent for chunking, that creates a cycle

The solution is to move `TokenUsage` to the agent package (it's agent-specific anyway), then:
- `agent` exports chunking functions and TokenUsage
- `checkpoint` imports `agent` for chunking
- No cycle

    43→
    44→// Type indicates the storage location and lifecycle of a checkpoint.
    45→type Type int
    46→
    47→const (
    48→	// Temporary checkpoints contain full state (code + metadata) and are stored
    49→	// on shadow branches (entire/<commit-hash>). Used for intra-session rewind.
    50→	Temporary Type = iota
    51→
    52→	// Committed checkpoints contain metadata + commit reference and are stored
    53→	// on the entire/sessions branch. They are the permanent record.
    54→	Committed
    55→)
    56→
    57→// Store provides low-level primitives for reading and writing checkpoints.
    58→// This is used by strategies to implement their storage approach.
    59→//
    60→// The interface matches the GitStore implementation signatures directly:
    61→// - WriteTemporary takes WriteTemporaryOptions and returns a result with commit hash and skip status
    62→// - ReadTemporary takes baseCommit (not sessionID) since shadow branches are keyed by commit
    63→// - List methods return implementation-specific info types for richer data
    64→type Store interface {
    65→	// WriteTemporary writes a temporary checkpoint (full state) to a shadow branch.
    66→	// Shadow branches are named entire/<base-commit-short-hash>.
    67→	// Returns a result containing the commit hash and whether the checkpoint was skipped.
    68→	// Checkpoints are skipped (deduplicated) when the tree hash matches the previous checkpoint.
    69→	WriteTemporary(ctx context.Context, opts WriteTemporaryOptions) (WriteTemporaryResult, error)
    70→
    71→	// ReadTemporary reads the latest checkpoint from a shadow branch.
    72→	// baseCommit is the commit hash the session is based on.
    73→	// Returns nil, nil if the shadow branch doesn't exist.
    74→	ReadTemporary(ctx context.Context, baseCommit string) (*ReadTemporaryResult, error)
    75→
    76→	// ListTemporary lists all shadow branches with their checkpoint info.
    77→	ListTemporary(ctx context.Context) ([]TemporaryInfo, error)
    78→
    79→	// WriteCommitted writes a committed checkpoint to the entire/sessions branch.
    80→	// Checkpoints are stored at sharded paths: <id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/
    81→	WriteCommitted(ctx context.Context, opts WriteCommittedOptions) error
    82→
    83→	// ReadCommitted reads a committed checkpoint by ID.
    84→	// Returns nil, nil if the checkpoint does not exist.
    85→	ReadCommitted(ctx context.Context, checkpointID string) (*ReadCommittedResult, error)
    86→
    87→	// ListCommitted lists all committed checkpoints.
    88→	ListCommitted(ctx context.Context) ([]CommittedInfo, error)
    89→}

    17→// Register adds an agent factory to the registry.

    19→func Register(name string, factory Factory) {

    21→	defer registryMu.Unlock()

    25→// Get retrieves an agent by name.

    27→//nolint:ireturn // Factory pattern requires returning the interface
    28→func Get(name string) (Agent, error) {
    29→	registryMu.RLock()
    30→	defer registryMu.RUnlock()
    31→
    32→	factory, ok := registry[name]
    33→	if !ok {

    36→	return factory(), nil

    43→

  "new_string": "// TranscriptAnalyzer is implemented by agents that support transcript analysis.\n// This allows agent-agnostic detection of work done between checkpoints.\ntype TranscriptAnalyzer interface {\n\tAgent\n\n\t// GetTranscriptPosition returns the current position (length) of a transcript.\n\t// For JSONL formats (Claude Code), this is the line count.\n\t// For JSON formats (Gemini CLI), this is the message count.\n\t// Returns 0 if the file doesn't exist or is empty.\n\t// Use this to efficiently check if the transcript has grown since last checkpoint.\n\tGetTranscriptPosition(path string) (int, error)\n\n\t// ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset extracts files modified since a given offset.\n\t// For JSONL formats (Claude Code), offset is the starting line number.\n\t// For JSON formats (Gemini CLI), offset is the starting message index.\n\t// Returns:\n\t//   - files: list of file paths modified by the agent (from Write/Edit tools)\n\t//   - currentPosition: the current position (line count or message count)\n\t//   - error: any error encountered during reading\n\tExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(path string, startOffset int) (files []string, currentPosition int, err error)\n}\n\n// TranscriptChunker is implemented by agents that support transcript chunking.\n// This allows agents to split large transcripts into chunks for storage (GitHub has\n// a 100MB blob limit) and reassemble them when reading.\ntype TranscriptChunker interface {\n\tAgent\n\n\t// ChunkTranscript splits a transcript into chunks if it exceeds maxSize.\n\t// Returns a slice of chunks. If the transcript fits in one chunk, returns single-element slice.\n\t// The chunking is format-aware: JSONL splits at line boundaries, JSON splits message arrays.\n\tChunkTranscript(content []byte, maxSize int) ([][]byte, error)\n\n\t// ReassembleTranscript combines chunks back into a single transcript.\n\t// Handles format-specific reassembly (JSONL concatenation, JSON message merging).\n\tReassembleTranscript(chunks [][]byte) ([]byte, error)\n}"

blob, so we use 50MB to be safe.\n\tMaxChunkSize = 50 * 1024 * 1024 // 50MB\n\n\t// ChunkSuffix is the format for chunk file suffixes (e.g., \".001\", \".002\")\n\tChunkSuffix = \".%03d\"\n)\n\n// ChunkTranscript splits a transcript into chunks using the appropriate agent.\n// If agentType is empty or the agent doesn't implement TranscriptChunker,\n// falls back to JSONL (line-based) chunking.\nfunc ChunkTranscript(content []byte, agentType string) ([][]byte, error) {\n\tif len(content) <= MaxChunkSize {\n\t\treturn [][]byte{content}, nil\n\t}\n\n\t// Try to get the agent by type\n\tif agentType != \"\" {\n\t\tag, err := GetByAgentType(agentType)\n\t\tif err == nil {\n\t\t\tif chunker, ok := ag.(TranscriptChunker); ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn chunker.ChunkTranscript(content, MaxChunkSize)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Fall back to JSONL chunking (default)\n\treturn ChunkJSONL(content, MaxChunkSize)\n}\n\n// ReassembleTranscript combines chunks back into a single transcript.\n// If agentType is empty or the agent doesn't implement TranscriptChunker,\n// falls back to JSONL (line-based) reassembly.\nfunc ReassembleTranscript(chunks [][]byte, agentType string) ([]byte, error) {\n\tif len(chunks) == 0 {\n\t\treturn nil, nil\n\t}\n\tif len(chunks) == 1 {\n\t\treturn chunks[0], nil\n\t}\n\n\t// Try to get the agent by type\n\tif agentType != \"\" {\n\t\tag, err := GetByAgentType(agentType)\n\t\tif err == nil {\n\t\t\tif chunker, ok := ag.(TranscriptChunker); ok {\n\t\t\t\treturn chunker.ReassembleTranscript(chunks)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\t// Fall back to JSONL reassembly (default)\n\treturn ReassembleJSONL(chunks), nil\n}\n\n// ChunkJSONL splits JSONL content at line boundaries.\n// This is the default chunking for agents using JSONL format (like Claude Code).\nfunc ChunkJSONL(content []byte, maxSize int) ([][]byte, error) {\n\tlines := strings.Split(string(content), \"\\n\")\n\tvar chunks [][]byte\n\tvar currentChunk strings.Builder\n\n\tfor _, line := range lines {\n\t\t// Check if adding this line would exceed the chunk size\n\t\tlineWithNewline := line + \"\\n\"\n\t\tif currentChunk.Len()+len(lineWithNewline) > maxSize && currentChunk.Len() > 0 {\n\t\t\t// Save current chunk and start a new one\n\t\t\tchunks = append(chunks, []byte(strings.TrimSuffix(currentChunk.String(), \"\\n\")))\n\t\t\tcurrentChunk.Reset()\n\t\t}\n\t\tcurrentChunk.WriteString(lineWithNewline)\n\t}\n\n\t// Add the last chunk if it has content\n\tif currentChunk.Len() > 0 {\n\t\tchunks = append(chunks, []byte(strings.TrimSuffix(currentChunk.String(), \"\\n\")))\n\t}\n\n\treturn chunks, nil\n}\n\n// ReassembleJSONL concatenates JSONL chunks with newlines.\nfunc ReassembleJSONL(chunks [][]byte) []byte {\n\tvar result strings.Builder\n\tfor i, chunk := range chunks {\n\t\tresult.Write(chunk)\n\t\tif i < len(chunks)-1 {\n\t\t\tresult.WriteString(\"\\n\")\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn []byte(result.String())\n}\n\n// ChunkFileName returns the filename for a chunk at the given index.\n// Index 0 returns the base filename, index 1+ returns with chunk suffix.\nfunc ChunkFileName(baseName string, index int) string {\n\tif index == 0 {\n\t\treturn baseName\n\t}\n\treturn baseName + fmt.Sprintf(ChunkSuffix, index)\n}\n\n// ParseChunkIndex extracts the chunk index from a filename.\n// Returns 0 for the base file (no suffix), or the chunk number for suffixed files.\n// Returns -1 if the filename doesn't match the expected pattern.\nfunc ParseChunkIndex(filename, baseName string) int {\n\tif filename == baseName {\n\t\treturn 0\n\t}\n\n\tif !strings.HasPrefix(filename, baseName+\".\") {\n\t\treturn -1\n\t}\n\n\tsuffix := strings.TrimPrefix(filename, baseName+\".\")\n\tvar index int\n\tif _, err := fmt.Sscanf(suffix, \"%03d\", &index); err != nil {\n\t\treturn -1\n\t}\n\treturn index\n}\n\n// SortChunkFiles sorts chunk filenames in order (base file first, then numbered chunks).\nfunc SortChunkFiles(files []string, baseName string) []string {\n\tsorted := make([]string, len(files))\n\tcopy(sorted, files)\n\n\tsort.Slice(sorted, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\tidxI := ParseChunkIndex(sorted[i], baseName)\n\t\tidxJ := ParseChunkIndex(sorted[j], baseName)\n\t\treturn idxI < idxJ\n\t})\n\n\treturn sorted\n}\n"
}

    77→// ParseHookInput parses Claude Code hook input from stdin.
    78→func (c *ClaudeCodeAgent) ParseHookInput(hookType agent.HookType, reader io.Reader) (*agent.HookInput, error) {
    79→	data, err := io.ReadAll(reader)
    80→	if err != nil {
    81→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read input: %w", err)
    82→	}

    97→		var raw sessionInfoRaw

    99→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse session info: %w", err)
   100→		}
   101→		input.SessionID = raw.SessionID
   102→		input.SessionRef = raw.TranscriptPath
   103→
   104→	case agent.HookPreToolUse:

   108→		}
   109→		input.SessionID = raw.SessionID
   110→		input.SessionRef = raw.TranscriptPath
   111→		input.ToolUseID = raw.ToolUseID
   112→		input.ToolInput = raw.ToolInput
   113→
   114→	case agent.HookPostToolUse:

   117→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse post-tool input: %w", err)
   118→		}
   119→		input.SessionID = raw.SessionID
   120→		input.SessionRef = raw.TranscriptPath
   121→		input.ToolUseID = raw.ToolUseID
   122→		input.ToolInput = raw.ToolInput
   123→		// Store agent ID in raw data for Task tool results
   124→		if raw.ToolResponse.AgentID != "" {

   126→		}
   127→	}

   173→	if input.SessionRef == "" {

   199→// WriteSession writes a session to Claude's storage (JSONL transcript file).

   202→func (c *ClaudeCodeAgent) WriteSession(session *agent.AgentSession) error {
   203→	if session == nil {

   205→	}
   206→
   207→	// Verify this session belongs to Claude Code
   208→	if session.AgentName != "" && session.AgentName != c.Name() {

   214→	}
   215→
   216→	if len(session.NativeData) == 0 {
   217→		return errors.New("session has no native data to write")
   218→	}

   222→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write transcript: %w", err)
   223→	}

   226→}

   250→// TruncateAtUUID returns a new session truncated at the given UUID (inclusive).
   251→// This is used for rewind operations to restore transcript state.
   252→// Requires NativeData to be populated.
   253→func (c *ClaudeCodeAgent) TruncateAtUUID(session *agent.AgentSession, uuid string) (*agent.AgentSession, error) {
   254→	if session == nil {
   255→		return nil, errors.New("session is nil")
   256→	}
   257→
   258→	if len(session.NativeData) == 0 {
   259→		return nil, errors.New("session has no native data")
   260→	}
   261→
   262→	if uuid == "" {
   263→		// No truncation needed, return copy
   264→		return &agent.AgentSession{

   266→			AgentName:     session.AgentName,
   267→			RepoPath:      session.RepoPath,
   268→			SessionRef:    session.SessionRef,
   269→			StartTime:     session.StartTime,
   270→			NativeData:    session.NativeData,
   271→			ModifiedFiles: session.ModifiedFiles,
   272→		}, nil
   273→	}
   274→
   275→	// Parse, truncate, re-serialize
   276→	lines, err := ParseTranscript(session.NativeData)
   277→	if err != nil {
   278→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse transcript: %w", err)
   279→	}
   280→
   281→	truncated := TruncateAtUUID(lines, uuid)

   283→	newData, err := SerializeTranscript(truncated)
   284→	if err != nil {
   285→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to serialize truncated transcript: %w", err)
   286→	}
   287→
   288→	return &agent.AgentSession{

   290→		AgentName:     session.AgentName,
   291→		RepoPath:      session.RepoPath,
   292→		SessionRef:    session.SessionRef,
   293→		StartTime:     session.StartTime,
   294→		NativeData:    newData,
   295→		ModifiedFiles: ExtractModifiedFiles(truncated),
   296→	}, nil
   297→}

   332→// TranscriptAnalyzer interface implementation
   333→
   334→// GetTranscriptPosition returns the current line count of a Claude Code transcript.
   335→// Claude Code uses JSONL format, so position is the number of lines.
   336→// This is a lightweight operation that only counts lines without parsing JSON.
   337→// Uses bufio.Reader to handle arbitrarily long lines (no size limit).
   338→// Returns 0 if the file doesn't exist or is empty.
   339→func (c *ClaudeCodeAgent) GetTranscriptPosition(path string) (int, error) {
   340→	if path == "" {
   341→		return 0, nil
   342→	}
   343→
   344→	file, err := os.Open(path) //nolint:gosec // Path comes from Claude Code transcript location
   345→	if err != nil {
   346→		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   347→			return 0, nil
   348→		}
   349→		return 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to open transcript file: %w", err)
   350→	}
   351→	defer file.Close()
   352→
   353→	reader := bufio.NewReader(file)
   354→	lineCount := 0
   355→
   356→	for {
   357→		_, err := reader.ReadBytes('\n')
   358→		if err != nil {
   359→			if err == io.EOF {
   360→				break
   361→			}
   362→			return 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to read transcript: %w", err)
   363→		}
   364→		lineCount++
   365→	}
   366→
   367→	return lineCount, nil
   368→}

   370→// ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset extracts files modified since a given line number.
   371→// For Claude Code (JSONL format), offset is the starting line number.
   372→// Uses bufio.Reader to handle arbitrarily long lines (no size limit).
   373→// Returns:
   374→//   - files: list of file paths modified by Claude (from Write/Edit tools)
   375→//   - currentPosition: total number of lines in the file
   376→//   - error: any error encountered during reading
   377→func (c *ClaudeCodeAgent) ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(path string, startOffset int) (files []string, currentPosition int, err error) {
   378→	if path == "" {
   379→		return nil, 0, nil
   380→	}
   381→
   382→	file, openErr := os.Open(path) //nolint:gosec // Path comes from Claude Code transcript location
   383→	if openErr != nil {
   384→		return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to open transcript file: %w", openErr)
   385→	}
   386→	defer file.Close()
   387→
   388→	reader := bufio.NewReader(file)
   389→	var lines []TranscriptLine
   390→	lineNum := 0
   391→
   392→	for {
   393→		lineData, readErr := reader.ReadBytes('\n')
   394→		if readErr != nil && readErr != io.EOF {
   395→			return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to read transcript: %w", readErr)
   396→		}
   397→
   398→		if len(lineData) > 0 {
   399→			lineNum++
   400→			if lineNum > startOffset {
   401→				var line TranscriptLine
   402→				if parseErr := json.Unmarshal(lineData, &line); parseErr == nil {
   403→					lines = append(lines, line)
   404→				}
   405→				// Skip malformed lines silently
   406→			}
   407→		}
   408→
   409→		if readErr == io.EOF {
   410→			break
   411→		}
   412→	}
   413→
   414→	return ExtractModifiedFiles(lines), lineNum, nil
   415→}

    76→func (g *GeminiCLIAgent) ParseHookInput(hookType agent.HookType, reader io.Reader) (*agent.HookInput, error) {
    77→	data, err := io.ReadAll(reader)

    95→		var raw sessionInfoRaw

    99→		input.SessionID = raw.SessionID

   114→		var raw agentHookInputRaw
   115→		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &raw); err != nil {
   116→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse agent hook input: %w", err)
   117→		}
   118→		input.SessionID = raw.SessionID
   119→		input.SessionRef = raw.TranscriptPath
   120→		input.RawData["cwd"] = raw.Cwd
   121→		input.RawData["hook_event_name"] = raw.HookEventName
   122→		if raw.Prompt != "" {
   123→			input.UserPrompt = raw.Prompt
   124→			input.RawData["prompt"] = raw.Prompt
   125→		}

   127→	case agent.HookPreToolUse, agent.HookPostToolUse:

   133→		input.SessionRef = raw.TranscriptPath

   215→// WriteSession writes a session to Gemini's storage (JSON transcript file).
   216→// Uses the NativeData field which contains raw JSON bytes.
   217→func (g *GeminiCLIAgent) WriteSession(session *agent.AgentSession) error {
   218→	if session == nil {
   219→		return errors.New("session is nil")
   220→	}
   221→
   222→	// Verify this session belongs to Gemini CLI
   223→	if session.AgentName != "" && session.AgentName != g.Name() {
   224→		return fmt.Errorf("session belongs to agent %q, not %q", session.AgentName, g.Name())
   225→	}
   226→
   227→	if session.SessionRef == "" {
   228→		return errors.New("session reference (transcript path) is required")
   229→	}
   230→
   231→	if len(session.NativeData) == 0 {
   232→		return errors.New("session has no native data to write")
   233→	}
   234→
   235→	// Write the raw JSON data
   236→	if err := os.WriteFile(session.SessionRef, session.NativeData, 0o600); err != nil {
   237→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write transcript: %w", err)
   238→	}
   239→
   240→	return nil
   241→}

   286→// ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset extracts files modified since a given message index.

   292→func (g *GeminiCLIAgent) ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(path string, startOffset int) (files []string, currentPosition int, err error) {
   293→	if path == "" {
   294→		return nil, 0, nil
   295→	}
   296→
   297→	data, readErr := os.ReadFile(path) //nolint:gosec // Reading from controlled transcript path
   298→	if readErr != nil {

   300→			return nil, 0, nil
   301→		}
   302→		return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to read transcript: %w", readErr)
   303→	}
   304→
   305→	if len(data) == 0 {
   306→		return nil, 0, nil
   307→	}
   308→
   309→	transcript, parseErr := ParseTranscript(data)
   310→	if parseErr != nil {
   311→		return nil, 0, parseErr
   312→	}

   314→	totalMessages := len(transcript.Messages)

   316→	// Extract files from messages starting at startOffset
   317→	fileSet := make(map[string]bool)
   318→	for i := startOffset; i < len(transcript.Messages); i++ {

   321→		if msg.Type != MessageTypeGemini {
   322→			continue
   323→		}

   326→		for _, toolCall := range msg.ToolCalls {

   328→			isModifyTool := false
   329→			for _, name := range FileModificationTools {

   333→				}
   334→			}
   335→
   336→			if !isModifyTool {
   337→				continue
   338→			}
   339→
   340→			// Extract file path from args map
   341→			var file string
   342→			if fp, ok := toolCall.Args["file_path"].(string); ok && fp != "" {
   343→				file = fp
   344→			} else if p, ok := toolCall.Args["path"].(string); ok && p != "" {
   345→				file = p
   346→			} else if fn, ok := toolCall.Args["filename"].(string); ok && fn != "" {
   347→				file = fn
   348→			}

   350→			if file != "" && !fileSet[file] {

  "old_string": "// SortChunkFiles sorts chunk filenames in order (base file first, then numbered chunks).\nfunc SortChunkFiles(files []string, baseName string) []string {\n\tsorted := make([]string, len(files))\n\tcopy(sorted, files)\n\n\tsort.Slice(sorted, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\tidxI := ParseChunkIndex(sorted[i], baseName)\n\t\tidxJ := ParseChunkIndex(sorted[j], baseName)\n\t\treturn idxI < idxJ\n\t})\n\n\treturn sorted\n}",
  "new_string": "// SortChunkFiles sorts chunk filenames in order (base file first, then numbered chunks).\nfunc SortChunkFiles(files []string, baseName string) []string {\n\tsorted := make([]string, len(files))\n\tcopy(sorted, files)\n\n\tsort.Slice(sorted, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\tidxI := ParseChunkIndex(sorted[i], baseName)\n\t\tidxJ := ParseChunkIndex(sorted[j], baseName)\n\t\treturn idxI < idxJ\n\t})\n\n\treturn sorted\n}\n\n// DetectAgentTypeFromContent detects the agent type from transcript content.\n// Returns \"Gemini CLI\" if it appears to be Gemini JSON format, empty string otherwise.\n// This is used when the agent type is unknown but we need to chunk/reassemble correctly.\nfunc DetectAgentTypeFromContent(content []byte) string {\n\t// Quick check: Gemini JSON starts with { and has a messages array\n\ttrimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(content))\n\tif !strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, \"{\") {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\n\t// Try to get Gemini agent and check if it can parse the content\n\tag, err := Get(AgentNameGemini)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn \"\"\n\t}\n\n\t// Type assert to check if it's a valid Gemini transcript\n\tif chunker, ok := ag.(TranscriptChunker); ok {\n\t\t// Try chunking with a very large maxSize - if it succeeds without error,\n\t\t// and we get back the same content, it's valid Gemini JSON\n\t\t_, chunkErr := chunker.ChunkTranscript(content, len(content)+1)\n\t\tif chunkErr == nil {\n\t\t\treturn \"Gemini CLI\"\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\n\treturn \"\"\n}"
}

> AGENT

All tests pass and linting shows 0 issues. Here's a summary of the refactoring:

## Summary

Moved transcript chunking into the agent package, so each agent owns its format-specific chunking logic.

### New Files

**`agent/chunking.go`** - Package-level chunking utilities:
- `ChunkTranscript(content, agentType)` - dispatches to registered agent or falls back to JSONL
- `ReassembleTranscript(chunks, agentType)` - dispatches to registered agent or falls back to JSONL
- `ChunkJSONL(content, maxSize)` / `ReassembleJSONL(chunks)` - default JSONL implementation
- `ChunkFileName()`, `ParseChunkIndex()`, `SortChunkFiles()` - file naming utilities
- `DetectAgentTypeFromContent()` - detects Gemini JSON format from content

**`agent/chunking_test.go`** - Tests for chunking utilities

### Modified Files

**`agent/agent.go`** - Added `TranscriptChunker` interface:
```go
type TranscriptChunker interface {
    Agent
    ChunkTranscript(content []byte, maxSize int) ([][]byte, error)
    ReassembleTranscript(chunks [][]byte) ([]byte, error)
}
```

**`agent/claudecode/claude.go`** - Implements `TranscriptChunker`:

   284→// accumulateTokenUsage adds new token usage to existing accumulated usage.
   285→// If existing is nil, returns a copy of incoming. If incoming is nil, returns existing unchanged.
   286→func accumulateTokenUsage(existing, incoming *checkpoint.TokenUsage) *checkpoint.TokenUsage {
   287→	if incoming == nil {
   288→		return existing
   289→	}
   290→	if existing == nil {
   291→		// Return a copy to avoid sharing the pointer
   292→		return &checkpoint.TokenUsage{
   293→			InputTokens:         incoming.InputTokens,
   294→			CacheCreationTokens: incoming.CacheCreationTokens,
   295→			CacheReadTokens:     incoming.CacheReadTokens,
   296→			OutputTokens:        incoming.OutputTokens,
   297→			APICallCount:        incoming.APICallCount,
   298→			SubagentTokens:      incoming.SubagentTokens,
   299→		}
   300→	}
   301→
   302→	// Accumulate values
   303→	existing.InputTokens += incoming.InputTokens
   304→	existing.CacheCreationTokens += incoming.CacheCreationTokens
   305→	existing.CacheReadTokens += incoming.CacheReadTokens

     1→package geminicli
     2→
     3→import (
     4→	"encoding/json"
     5→	"fmt"
     6→	"os"
     7→)
     8→
     9→// Transcript parsing types - Gemini CLI uses JSON format for session storage
    10→// Based on transcript_path format: ~/.gemini/tmp/<hash>/chats/session-<date>-<id>.json
    11→
    12→// Message type constants for Gemini transcripts
    13→const (
    14→	MessageTypeUser   = "user"
    15→	MessageTypeGemini = "gemini"
    16→)
    17→
    18→// GeminiTranscript represents the top-level structure of a Gemini session file
    19→type GeminiTranscript struct {
    20→	Messages []GeminiMessage `json:"messages"`
    21→}
    22→
    23→// GeminiMessage represents a single message in the transcript
    24→type GeminiMessage struct {
    25→	Type      string           `json:"type"` // MessageTypeUser or MessageTypeGemini
    26→	Content   string           `json:"content,omitempty"`
    27→	ToolCalls []GeminiToolCall `json:"toolCalls,omitempty"`
    28→}
    29→
    30→// GeminiToolCall represents a tool call in a gemini message
    31→type GeminiToolCall struct {
    32→	ID     string                 `json:"id"`
    33→	Name   string                 `json:"name"`
    34→	Args   map[string]interface{} `json:"args"`
    35→	Status string                 `json:"status,omitempty"`
    36→}
    37→
    38→// ParseTranscript parses raw JSON content into a transcript structure
    39→func ParseTranscript(data []byte) (*GeminiTranscript, error) {
    40→	var transcript GeminiTranscript
    41→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &transcript); err != nil {
    42→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse transcript: %w", err)
    43→	}
    44→	return &transcript, nil
    45→}
    46→
    47→// ExtractModifiedFiles extracts files modified by tool calls from transcript data
    48→func ExtractModifiedFiles(data []byte) ([]string, error) {
    49→	transcript, err := ParseTranscript(data)
    50→	if err != nil {
    51→		return nil, err
    52→	}
    53→
    54→	return ExtractModifiedFilesFromTranscript(transcript), nil
    55→}
    56→
    57→// ExtractModifiedFilesFromTranscript extracts files from a parsed transcript
    58→func ExtractModifiedFilesFromTranscript(transcript *GeminiTranscript) []string {
    59→	fileSet := make(map[string]bool)
    60→	var files []string
    61→
    62→	for _, msg := range transcript.Messages {
    63→		// Only process gemini messages (assistant messages)
    64→		if msg.Type != MessageTypeGemini {
    65→			continue
    66→		}
    67→
    68→		// Process tool calls in this message
    69→		for _, toolCall := range msg.ToolCalls {
    70→			// Check if it's a file modification tool
    71→			isModifyTool := false
    72→			for _, name := range FileModificationTools {
    73→				if toolCall.Name == name {
    74→					isModifyTool = true
    75→					break
    76→				}
    77→			}
    78→
    79→			if !isModifyTool {
    80→				continue
    81→			}
    82→
    83→			// Extract file path from args map
    84→			var file string
    85→			if fp, ok := toolCall.Args["file_path"].(string); ok && fp != "" {
    86→				file = fp
    87→			} else if p, ok := toolCall.Args["path"].(string); ok && p != "" {
    88→				file = p
    89→			} else if fn, ok := toolCall.Args["filename"].(string); ok && fn != "" {
    90→				file = fn
    91→			}
    92→
    93→			if file != "" && !fileSet[file] {
    94→				fileSet[file] = true
    95→				files = append(files, file)
    96→			}
    97→		}
    98→	}
    99→
   100→	return files
   101→}
   102→
   103→// ExtractLastUserPrompt extracts the last user message from transcript data
   104→func ExtractLastUserPrompt(data []byte) (string, error) {
   105→	transcript, err := ParseTranscript(data)
   106→	if err != nil {
   107→		return "", err
   108→	}
   109→
   110→	return ExtractLastUserPromptFromTranscript(transcript), nil
   111→}
   112→
   113→// ExtractLastUserPromptFromTranscript extracts the last user prompt from a parsed transcript
   114→func ExtractLastUserPromptFromTranscript(transcript *GeminiTranscript) string {
   115→	for i := len(transcript.Messages) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
   116→		msg := transcript.Messages[i]
   117→		if msg.Type != MessageTypeUser {
   118→			continue
   119→		}
   120→
   121→		// Content is now a string field
   122→		if msg.Content != "" {
   123→			return msg.Content
   124→		}
   125→	}
   126→	return ""
   127→}
   128→
   129→// ExtractAllUserPrompts extracts all user messages from transcript data
   130→func ExtractAllUserPrompts(data []byte) ([]string, error) {
   131→	transcript, err := ParseTranscript(data)
   132→	if err != nil {
   133→		return nil, err
   134→	}
   135→
   136→	return ExtractAllUserPromptsFromTranscript(transcript), nil
   137→}
   138→
   139→// ExtractAllUserPromptsFromTranscript extracts all user prompts from a parsed transcript
   140→func ExtractAllUserPromptsFromTranscript(transcript *GeminiTranscript) []string {
   141→	var prompts []string
   142→	for _, msg := range transcript.Messages {
   143→		if msg.Type == MessageTypeUser && msg.Content != "" {
   144→			prompts = append(prompts, msg.Content)
   145→		}
   146→	}
   147→	return prompts
   148→}
   149→
   150→// ExtractLastAssistantMessage extracts the last gemini response from transcript data
   151→func ExtractLastAssistantMessage(data []byte) (string, error) {
   152→	transcript, err := ParseTranscript(data)
   153→	if err != nil {
   154→		return "", err
   155→	}
   156→
   157→	return ExtractLastAssistantMessageFromTranscript(transcript), nil
   158→}
   159→
   160→// ExtractLastAssistantMessageFromTranscript extracts the last gemini response from a parsed transcript
   161→func ExtractLastAssistantMessageFromTranscript(transcript *GeminiTranscript) string {
   162→	for i := len(transcript.Messages) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
   163→		msg := transcript.Messages[i]
   164→		if msg.Type == MessageTypeGemini && msg.Content != "" {
   165→			return msg.Content
   166→		}
   167→	}
   168→	return ""
   169→}
   170→
   171→// TokenUsage represents aggregated token usage for a checkpoint
   172→type TokenUsage struct {
   173→	// InputTokens is the number of input tokens (fresh, not from cache)
   174→	InputTokens int `json:"input_tokens"`
   175→	// OutputTokens is the number of output tokens generated
   176→	OutputTokens int `json:"output_tokens"`
   177→	// CacheReadTokens is the number of tokens read from cache
   178→	CacheReadTokens int `json:"cache_read_tokens"`
   179→	// APICallCount is the number of API calls made
   180→	APICallCount int `json:"api_call_count"`
   181→}
   182→
   183→// CalculateTokenUsage calculates token usage from a Gemini transcript.
   184→// This is specific to Gemini's API format where each message may have a tokens object
   185→// with input, output, cached, thoughts, tool, and total counts.
   186→// Only processes messages from startMessageIndex onwards (0-indexed).
   187→func CalculateTokenUsage(data []byte, startMessageIndex int) *TokenUsage {
   188→	var transcript struct {
   189→		Messages []geminiMessageWithTokens `json:"messages"`
   190→	}
   191→
   192→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &transcript); err != nil {
   193→		return &TokenUsage{}
   194→	}
   195→
   196→	usage := &TokenUsage{}
   197→
   198→	for i, msg := range transcript.Messages {
   199→		// Skip messages before startMessageIndex
   200→		if i < startMessageIndex {
   201→			continue
   202→		}
   203→
   204→		// Only count tokens from gemini (assistant) messages
   205→		if msg.Type != MessageTypeGemini {
   206→			continue
   207→		}
   208→
   209→		if msg.Tokens == nil {
   210→			continue
   211→		}
   212→
   213→		usage.APICallCount++
   214→		usage.InputTokens += msg.Tokens.Input
   215→		usage.OutputTokens += msg.Tokens.Output
   216→		usage.CacheReadTokens += msg.Tokens.Cached
   217→	}
   218→
   219→	return usage
   220→}
   221→
   222→// CalculateTokenUsageFromFile calculates token usage from a Gemini transcript file.
   223→// If startMessageIndex > 0, only considers messages from that index onwards.
   224→func CalculateTokenUsageFromFile(path string, startMessageIndex int) (*TokenUsage, error) {
   225→	if path == "" {
   226→		return &TokenUsage{}, nil
   227→	}
   228→
   229→	data, err := os.ReadFile(path) //nolint:gosec // Reading from controlled transcript path
   230→	if err != nil {
   231→		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   232→			return &TokenUsage{}, nil
   233→		}
   234→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read transcript: %w", err)
   235→	}
   236→
   237→	return CalculateTokenUsage(data, startMessageIndex), nil
   238→}
   239→
